meta.purpose: Initial hierarchical scaffold identifying every merchandising fixture and non-merchandising space to draw as a 3D block in SketchUp Free. Geometry fields are null and get filled in after the OBJ export is parsed.
meta.units: feet — set SketchUp's Model Info > Units to feet before drawing
meta.coordinate_system: Draw the entire store in ONE shared SketchUp file/scene, at true scale, with each block positioned at its actual intended location on the store floor plan (not loose/unpositioned boxes). Ground plane = red/green (X/Y) axes, blue (Z) = height, origin at one corner of the store footprint (e.g. front entrance corner).
meta.naming_rule: Name every group in SketchUp EXACTLY as its 'sketchup_object_name' value below (underscores, no spaces/punctuation) — that name is the ONLY channel of metadata that survives OBJ export, and it's how extracted geometry gets matched back to this JSON. Use Groups (not Components) to avoid shared-definition name collisions when copying similar fixtures.
meta.drawing_rule: Each object = one rectangular 3D block (a SketchUp group or component) representing the fixture's overall footprint and height. Do NOT draw individual shelves — vertical shelf bands (see 'shelf_bands') are computed later by evenly subdividing each block's height.
meta.layout_notes: Ch. 1.3: perimeter placement for produce/meat/deli/bakery/dairy (flagged via 'perimeter_department' below) with center-store grocery in the interior aisles. Ch. 1.4: produce near the entrance, dairy toward the back to pull shoppers through center aisles. Ch. 1.5: grid aisle layout is dominant for supermarkets. These are placement guidelines for where YOU position each block, not computed coordinates.
